transcription.text:
Match the categories of AI with its correct description.
Categories of AI | Description
I. Artificial Narrow Intelligence | 1. Level of general and strong AI that is smarter than humans if that’s possible.
II. Artificial General Intelligence | 2. Such system seems to act intelligently but they don't have any awareness of what they are doing.
III. Super Intelligence | 3. Acting like a smart human and thinking like one with a conscious.
transcription.printedErrors: Description 3 ends 'with a conscious' where 'consciousness' is meant.
transcription.changes: added the match table (Categories of AI / Description), which was missing from the extracted text

subject: Computer Science
concept: Types of AI: ANI, AGI, ASI
explanation:
- **I. Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI, weak AI) → 2.** It is built for one specific task (voice assistants, spam filters, chess engines). It appears to act intelligently but has no understanding or awareness of what it is doing.
- **II. Artificial General Intelligence (AGI, strong AI) → 3.** A hypothetical system with human-level general intelligence: it would think, reason and learn across any domain like a smart human, with something like consciousness.
- **III. Super Intelligence (ASI) → 1.** A hypothetical level beyond general/strong AI, smarter than humans in every respect, if such a thing is possible at all.

So the matching is I-2, II-3, III-1, which is option A. The other options either give narrow AI human-like consciousness (I-1/I-3) or swap general AI with super intelligence.

transcription.text: Which of the following notation of ERD (Entity – Relationship Diagram) shows the ‘Weak Entity’?
options: [Figure: double rectangle (a rectangle inside a rectangle)]
transcription.figureDescription: The four options are ER-diagram shapes: a single rectangle, a diamond, a double rectangle and a double diamond.
transcription.changes: options were empty (images only); added descriptions of the four shapes

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
In Chen's ER notation:
- **Single rectangle**: a (strong) entity set
- **Diamond**: a relationship set
- **Double rectangle**: a **weak entity set**
- **Double diamond**: an identifying relationship, which links a weak entity to its owner (identifying) entity

A weak entity cannot be uniquely identified by its own attributes. It depends on an owner entity and has only a partial key (discriminator), drawn with a dashed underline. Example: DEPENDENT of an EMPLOYEE, identified by employee ID + dependent name.

So the weak entity is shown by the **double rectangle**, option C. The double diamond (option D) is closely related but represents the identifying relationship, not the weak entity itself.

transcription.text: Which of the following tag of HTML language is a container for the tags that contain information about the page?

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
The `<head>` element is the container for **metadata**, i.e. information about the page rather than content shown in the page. It holds tags such as `<title>`, `<meta>`, `<link>`, `<style>`, `<script>` and `<base>`.

```
<html>
  <head>
    <title>My Page</title>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
  </head>
  <body> ...visible content... </body>
</html>
```

Why not the others:
- `<title>` is one of the tags *inside* `<head>`; it is not a container for the others.
- `<html>` is the root element containing the whole document (both head and body).
- `<body>` contains the visible content of the page, not information about it.

So the answer is `<head>`, option C.

transcription.text: Which of the following logic gate is shown in the given Graphic Symbol? (where, A and B = inputs, x = output)
transcription.figureDescription: Gate symbol with inputs A and B and output x: an OR-gate shape with an extra curved line before its input side and no bubble at the output.

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
The symbol has the curved, pointed shape of an OR gate **plus an extra curved line** drawn just behind the input side, and **no bubble** at the output. That extra curve is the distinguishing mark of the **Exclusive-OR (XOR)** gate.

XOR output: x = A ⊕ B = A′B + AB′, which is 1 only when the inputs differ.
- A=0, B=0 → 0
- A=0, B=1 → 1
- A=1, B=0 → 1
- A=1, B=1 → 0

Why not the others:
- **OR gate**: same shape but without the extra input curve.
- **NOR gate**: OR shape with a small bubble (inversion circle) at the output.
- **NAND gate**: D-shaped AND body with a bubble at the output.

So the answer is option D.

transcription.text:
Match the following Process states of Operating System with their definitions.
State | Definition
I. New | 1. The process is waiting to be assigned to a processor
II. Running | 2. Instructions are being executed
III. Ready | 3. The process is being created
transcription.changes: de finitions→definitions; added the match table (State / Definition), which was missing from the extracted text

subject: Computer Science
explanation:
The standard five-state process model is New → Ready → Running → Waiting → Terminated.

- **I. New → 3.** The process is being created (PCB allocated, program loaded), but it has not yet been admitted to the ready queue.
- **II. Running → 2.** The CPU is currently executing the process's instructions.
- **III. Ready → 1.** The process has everything it needs except the CPU; it is waiting in the ready queue to be assigned to a processor by the scheduler.

So the matching is I-3, II-2, III-1, which is option D.

A common confusion is between Ready and Waiting (Blocked): a *waiting* process is waiting for an event such as I/O completion, whereas a *ready* process is waiting only for the CPU.

transcription.text:
Match the following Classification Of Cognitive Disability (Mental Retardation) with their range of intelligence quotient (IQ).
Severity Levels | Range of IQ
I. Profound Mentally Retarded | 1. 20-34
II. Mild Mentally Retarded | 2. Below 20
III. Severe Mentally Retarded | 3. 50-75
transcription.changes: added the match table (Severity Levels / Range of IQ), which was missing from the extracted text

subject: Teaching Methodology
explanation:
The classic IQ-based classification of intellectual disability (earlier called mental retardation) is roughly:
- **Mild**: about 50–70 (some sources give 50/55 to 70/75)
- **Moderate**: about 35–49
- **Severe**: about 20–34
- **Profound**: below 20

Matching:
- **I. Profound → 2 (Below 20)**
- **II. Mild → 3 (50–75)**, the highest of the given ranges
- **III. Severe → 1 (20–34)**

So the answer is I-2, II-3, III-1, option A.

Tip: severity goes up as IQ goes down, so the lowest range (below 20) is profound and the highest (50–75) is mild. Modern systems (DSM-5) grade severity mainly by adaptive functioning, but these IQ bands are still what teacher-eligibility exams test.

transcription.text: How many bikes are scooters?
transcription.figureDescription: Venn diagram with a circle (Scooter), a rectangle (Bike) and a right triangle (Car): Bike only 8, Scooter∩Bike only 16, all three 2, Bike∩Car only 1, Scooter only 4 and 1, Scooter∩Car only 3, Car only 4.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
explanation:
In the diagram: rectangle = Bike, circle = Scooter, triangle = Car.

'Bikes that are scooters' means every region common to the rectangle **and** the circle, whether or not it is also in the triangle:
- **16**: inside the rectangle and the circle, outside the triangle
- **2**: inside the rectangle, the circle and the triangle

Total = 16 + 2 = **18**.

Why not the others:
- 16 counts only the region outside the triangle and misses the 2 that are also cars.
- 17 and 19 come from wrongly adding the 1 (bike and car, not scooter) or a scooter-only region.

So the answer is 18, option B.

II. Total number of cartoon are 23.
transcription.figureDescription: Venn diagram with a vertical rectangle (Ball), a horizontal rectangle (Cartoon) and a triangle (Blue): Ball only 4, Cartoon∩Blue only 3, all three 16, Cartoon only 2, Blue only 8, Ball∩Blue only 4.

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
explanation:
Shapes: vertical rectangle = Ball, horizontal rectangle = Cartoon, triangle = Blue.

**Statement I:** balls that are not blue = regions of the vertical rectangle outside the triangle. Only the **4** at the top lies there (the rest of the ball rectangle that has numbers, 16 and the lower 4, is inside the triangle). So I is **correct**.

**Statement II:** total cartoons = all numbers inside the horizontal rectangle = 3 + 16 + 2 = **21**, not 23. So II is **not correct**.

transcription.text: Raman walks 25 metres in north. He turns right and walks 72 metres to reach point A. He again turns right and walks 16 metres. He finally turns left and walks 8 metres to reach point B. How far is point B from point A and in which direction is starting point from point B?

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
explanation:
Take the starting point O as (0, 0), with east = +x and north = +y.

- 25 m north → (0, 25)
- Turn right (now facing east), 72 m → **A = (72, 25)**
- Turn right again (now facing south), 16 m → (72, 9)
- Turn left (now facing east), 8 m → **B = (80, 9)**

**Distance AB:** horizontal gap 80 − 72 = 8, vertical gap 25 − 9 = 16.
AB = √(8² + 16²) = √(64 + 256) = **√320** m (= 8√5 ≈ 17.9 m).

**Direction of O from B:** O (0, 0) is to the left (west) and below (south) of B (80, 9), so the starting point is **South-West** of B.

Why not the others: √340 comes from an arithmetic slip, and North-East is the direction of B from O, the reverse of what is asked. So the answer is option D.

transcription.text: By folding the given paper, which of the following cube cannot be made?
transcription.figureDescription: Net: top row A, J, L; bottom row C, D, H, with C directly below L; cubes show I (top C, faces A, J), II (top L, faces J, H), III (top D, faces L, J), IV (top H, faces A, C).

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
explanation:
First find the opposite pairs from the net. In a straight row of three squares, the first and third are opposite.
- Row A J L → **A opposite L**
- Row C D H → **C opposite H**
- The remaining pair → **J opposite D**

Two opposite faces can never be seen together on a cube.

Check each cube:
- **I** (C, A, J): no opposite pair → can be made
- **II** (L, J, H): no opposite pair → can be made
- **III** (D, L, J): shows **J and D**, which are opposite → **cannot be made**
- **IV** (H, A, C): shows **C and H**, which are opposite → **cannot be made**

So cubes III and IV cannot be made, option B. Only option B contains both III and IV, so the other options are ruled out.

transcription.text: By folding the given paper, which of the following cube cannot be made?
transcription.figureDescription: Staircase net: * and % in the first row, @ (below %) and 7 in the second, 4 (below 7) and 3 in the third; cubes show I (top 3, faces *, %), II (top 3, faces 7, 4), III (top *, faces %, 4), IV (top 7, faces @, 3).

subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
keyNote: keysAcrossCopies lists 2021-set4-q040 with key D, but that paper's Q40 has a different net (A, 7, 6, 4, 3, 8) and different options, so it is a different question and is not a real key conflict.
explanation:
Fold the staircase net with @ as the base:
- % (above @) folds up as the back face, and * (left of %) becomes the left face.
- 7 (right of @) becomes the right face, 4 (below 7) becomes the front face, and 3 (right of 4) lands on top.

Opposite pairs: **@ – 3**, **% – 4**, **\* – 7**.

Check each cube (opposite faces can never be seen together):

- **II** (3, 7, 4): no opposite pair; order also matches → can be made

transcription.text: If A/B = 11/9, then what is the value of ((A − B)/(A + B))?
transcription.changes: rebuilt the garbled OCR of the fractions in the question; options '', 'I', '9\n20', '1\n20' → 9/10, 1/10, 9/20, 1/20

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
explanation:
Since A/B = 11/9, take A = 11k and B = 9k.

A − B = 11k − 9k = 2k
A + B = 11k + 9k = 20k

(A − B)/(A + B) = 2k / 20k = **1/10**

Shortcut: divide numerator and denominator by B:
(A/B − 1)/(A/B + 1) = (11/9 − 1)/(11/9 + 1) = (2/9)/(20/9) = 2/20 = 1/10.

Why not the others: 9/10 and 9/20 wrongly keep the 9 from B in the numerator, and 1/20 forgets to simplify 2/20. So the answer is option B.

transcription.text: Which of the following numbers will completely divide (7^29 − 7^30 − 7^31 + 7^32)?

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
concept: Divisibility of power expressions by factoring
explanation:
Take out the smallest power, 7²⁹:

7²⁹ − 7³⁰ − 7³¹ + 7³² = 7²⁹ (1 − 7 − 7² + 7³)
= 7²⁹ (1 − 7 − 49 + 343)
= 7²⁹ × **288**

Alternatively, factor in pairs: 1 − 7 − 49 + 343 = (1 − 7) − 49(1 − 7) = (1 − 7)(1 − 49) = (−6)(−48) = 288.

288 = 2⁵ × 3² and 7²⁹ has only the prime factor 7.

Check the options:
- **72** = 2³ × 3² → divides 288 (288 = 72 × 4) ✓
- 26 = 2 × 13 → needs 13 ✗
- 51 = 3 × 17 → needs 17 ✗
- 78 = 2 × 3 × 13 → needs 13 ✗

So the expression is divisible by 72, option C.

transcription.text: If a : b = 2 : 3, then what is the value of (b^2 + 2a^2) : (b^2 − 2a^2)?

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
explanation:
Let a = 2k and b = 3k.

b² + 2a² = 9k² + 2(4k²) = 9k² + 8k² = **17k²**
b² − 2a² = 9k² − 2(4k²) = 9k² − 8k² = **k²**

Ratio = 17k² : k² = **17 : 1**

Since k² cancels, you can simply put a = 2 and b = 3: (9 + 8) : (9 − 8) = 17 : 1.

Why not the others: 18 : 1 and 15 : 2 come from slips such as using 2a instead of 2a², and 20 : 11 does not follow from the given ratio. So the answer is option A.

transcription.text:
The table given below shows the price (in lakh) of six cars C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6 in three different cities X, Y and Z.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
I. The ratio of price of C1 in city X to the price of C4 in city Z is 6 : 7 respectively.
II. The ratio of price of C1 in the city X to the price of C4 in city Z is 7 : 6 respectively.
III. Price of C5 is 5 percent more in city Y than the price in city X.

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
concept: Table DI: ratio and percentage increase
explanation:
Read the needed values from the table:
- C1 in city X = 3.5 lakh
- C4 in city Z = 3.0 lakh
- C5: city X = 4.0 lakh, city Y = 4.2 lakh

**Statements I and II:** C1 (X) : C4 (Z) = 3.5 : 3.0 = 35 : 30 = **7 : 6**. So II is correct and I (6 : 7, the reverse) is wrong.

**Statement III:** increase from X to Y = 4.2 − 4.0 = 0.2 lakh.
Percentage = 0.2 / 4.0 × 100 = **5%**. So III is correct.

Correct statements: II and III, option B. 'All are correct' is impossible anyway, because I and II contradict each other.

transcription.text:
The line chart given below shows the marked price and selling price of six articles A, B, C, D, E and F.
discount = (Marked price − Selling price)
discount % = (Marked price − Selling price)/Marked price × 100
J1 = Value of sum of discount on articles C and D
J2 = Value of difference of discount on articles D and E
What is the value of J1 − J2?
transcription.figureDescription: Line chart for articles A–F: marked price 685, 565, 450, 362, 435, 395 and selling price 615, 525, 425, 318, 420, 350.
transcription.changes: removed chart labels picked up by OCR (685., 565, ... 'Marked Price -*-Selling Price'); rebuilt the discount % formula; Dand→D and

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
explanation:
Discount = Marked price − Selling price.

- C: 450 − 425 = **25**
- D: 362 − 318 = **44**
- E: 435 − 420 = **15**

J1 = discount on C + discount on D = 25 + 44 = **69**
J2 = discount on D − discount on E = 44 − 15 = **29**

J1 − J2 = 69 − 29 = **40**

Note that the discount % formula given in the question is not needed here; J1 and J2 use the discount amounts.

Why not the others: 69 is J1 alone, 29 is J2 alone, and 20 would come from a misread value. So the answer is 40, option C.

transcription.text:
The line chart given below shows the birth rate (per thousand persons) and death rate (per thousand persons) of countries P, Q, R and S in the year 2018.
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
I. Birth rate of country Q is 9.2 percent more than country R.
II. Birth rate of country R is 11.76 percent more than the birthrate of country S.
III. Birth rate of country Q is 32 percent more than the birth rate of country S.
transcription.figureDescription: Line chart for countries P, Q, R, S: birth rate 6.6, 8.3, 7.6, 6.8 and death rate 5.3, 6.6, 5.3, 4.8 (per thousand).

subject: Arithmetical & Numerical Ability
concept: Line chart DI: percentage more than
explanation:
Birth rates from the chart: P = 6.6, Q = 8.3, R = 7.6, S = 6.8.

'X is p% more than Y' means p = (X − Y)/Y × 100.

**I:** Q vs R = (8.3 − 7.6)/7.6 × 100 = 0.7/7.6 × 100 ≈ **9.21%** → correct (≈ 9.2%)

**II:** R vs S = (7.6 − 6.8)/6.8 × 100 = 0.8/6.8 × 100 ≈ **11.76%** → correct

**III:** Q vs S = (8.3 − 6.8)/6.8 × 100 = 1.5/6.8 × 100 ≈ **22.06%**, not 32% → incorrect

So statements I and II are correct, option C.

दिए गए वाक्य में से मध्यम पुरूष सर्वनाम ज्ञात किजिए।

subject: Hindi Language
explanation:
पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम तीन प्रकार के होते हैं:
- **उत्तम पुरुष**: बोलने वाला अपने लिए प्रयोग करे (मैं, हम, मुझे, हमें)

अन्य विकल्प क्यों गलत हैं:
- **उलूखल-उल्लू**: ‘उलूखल’ का तद्भव ‘ओखली’ है; ‘उल्लू’ का तत्सम ‘उलूक’ है।
- **कदा-कौन**: ‘कदा’ का तद्भव ‘कब’ है; ‘कौन’ का संबंध ‘कः पुनः’ से माना जाता है।
- **कर्कटक-ककड़ी**: ‘कर्कटक’ का तद्भव ‘केकड़ा’ है; ‘ककड़ी’ का तत्सम ‘कर्कटी’ माना जाता है।

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प D ‘उपवेष्टन-ओढ़ना’ है। (प्रश्न में ‘तद्भव’ के स्थान पर ‘तद्धव’ छपा है।)

transcription.text:
दिए गए शब्द का विलोम शब्द ज्ञात कीजिए।
अग्रज

subject: Hindi Language
explanation:
‘**अग्रज**’ = अग्र (पहले/आगे) + ज (जन्मा), अर्थात जो पहले जन्मा हो: बड़ा भाई। इसका विलोम है ‘**अनुज**’ = अनु (पीछे/बाद में) + ज (जन्मा), अर्थात जो बाद में जन्मा हो: छोटा भाई।

अग्रज × अनुज

अन्य विकल्प क्यों गलत हैं:
- **कग्रज**: यह हिंदी का कोई मानक शब्द नहीं है।
- **ससीम**: सीमा सहित; इसका विलोम ‘असीम’ है।
- **अनघ**: पाप-रहित, निष्पाप; इसका विलोम ‘पापी’ या ‘सपाप’ जैसा शब्द होगा।

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प B ‘अनुज’ है।
